About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

At RobCo, we don’t just build robots, we are redefining the relationship between hardware and AI. Our end-to-end solutions seamlessly combine advanced, scalable industrial hardware with a central software suite powered by Physical AI to make manufacturing truly autonomous, efficient, and scalable. By delivering field-ready robotic solutions that just work, we empower industrial companies to automate without complexity and successfully solve the global labor shortage.

At RobCo, we automate the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary. To achieve this, we are looking for an ambitious Engineering Manager - Control & Low-Level Software (m/f/d) to help us establish RobCo as a leading provider of automation solutions.

In this key role, you will lead the team behind how our robots move: RobControl, the real-time controller running on every RobCo robot, together with control unit software, robot modeling and hardware integration. One controller codebase drives our modular robots, OEM configurations and Alfie, our autonomous industrial robot, so your team's work reaches every robot in the field. Managing a team of control, embedded and software engineers, you will balance new capabilities for Alfie and our physical AI roadmap with the reliability factory customers expect on every shift.

Your Responsibilities

  • Own the hardware-software bridge: Lead the team developing our real-time controller, robot models, hardware interfacing via EtherCat, as well as core robot algorithms like motion generation and planning, calibration, etc., running on Linux-based Control Units.

  • Lead and Grow the Team: Act as a people-first leader for a mixed team of experienced engineers and early-career talent. Hire and coach, and balance roadmap work with field support through clear priorities and a fair on-call rotation.

  • Drive Engineering Excellence: Set standards for code quality, hardware-in-the-loop and automated testing, and CI/CD, so that done means tested, released and running in the field. Improve observability so field issues can be diagnosed remotely and quickly.

  • One Platform for Every Robot: Keep one controller codebase for modular robots, OEM configurations and Alfie, extending it to new kinematic structures, more joints and multi-arm systems without forking it. Manage technical debt and architectural health as we scale.

  • Partner Across Teams: Work with Product Management, Hardware, Safety & Compliance and Robot Intelligence to turn customer and autonomy needs into a clear roadmap, integrate RobControl with the safety controller, and support certification against ISO 10218 and ISO 13849.

  • Cross-Team Leadership: Mentor junior EMs and help evolve company-wide engineering best practices and software-first principles.

We're looking for someone who has:

  • Completed a university degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field.

  • 3+ years of experience leading engineering teams that ship real-time or embedded software for robots, motion systems or other industrial machines.

  • Deep experience in robot control and motion is a big plus: kinematics and dynamics, trajectory generation, and position, velocity and torque control. Strong C++ and Python on real-time Linux, with hands-on EtherCAT and ROS 2 experience.

  • Proven track record of driving an AI-first engineering culture and implementing agentic workflows that measurably accelerate team velocity and system efficiency.

  • Expert knowledge of modern SDLC practices for software that runs on hardware, including hardware-in-the-loop testing and staged releases, with a track record of improving release frequency and field stability.

  • Working knowledge of functional safety for industrial robots (ISO 10218, ISO 13849) and experience working closely with safety and certification teams.

  • Culture-aligned mindset characterized by hardware empathy, a passion for software-defined hardware, and a strong culture of high ownership.

  • Very good English skills with the ability to navigate complex architectural discussions with Staff engineers while clearly communicating risks to stakeholders.

Why join RobCo?

  • Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.

  • Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.

  • As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.

  • Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.

  • Work out across Germany in over 7,200 studios with our subsidized Wellpass membership.

  • Flexible working hours, a modern office, and—depending on the role—the option to work from home.

  • Regular team events—from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.

About RobCo

Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that continuously learns and improves, requiring zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. In October 2026, RobCo reached unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion US dollars, with its valuation doubling in less than nine months. With $200M raised from investors including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto, Kindred, Cherry Ventures, and the European Tech Collective, 225+ people globally, and 3.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our Bay Area Lab in San Francisco.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements.

title: Research Software Engineering Intern (f/m/d)
description:
Description

QuantumDiamonds is building the world’s first commercial quantum sensing tools for chip failure analysis. As our Research Software Engineering Intern in Pre-Development, you bring our measurement software together. A measurement protocol is the recipe our Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDm) follows for one measurement: how laser, microwaves and camera are sequenced and timed, and how raw camera frames become a magnetic field image of a chip. Our engineers write new protocols whenever they test a new idea, and several backends for running them grew in parallel. You turn them into one shared Python framework that our engineers extend.

The challenge is a framework R&D still uses long after your internship: flexible enough that a new protocol is a day’s work, automated enough that a measurement runs without someone watching it, and structured enough that the next engineer extends it without reading all of it. An experienced colleague from the team mentors you and sets the architecture; you make that trade-off real in code, working with Claude Code every day, as our engineers do.

This is a full-time internship for 6 months, during or after your studies, starting as soon as possible.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

 
 

What will you do

  • Bring the measurement software of Pre-Development together into one shared Python framework, to a target architecture your mentor defines, and migrate the existing measurement protocols onto it.

  • Keep the CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions healthy as the framework grows: tests, linting, packaging, releases.

  • Give first-pass reviews on pull requests from our engineers (tests, conventions, API conformance) before your mentor approves them.

  • Help our engineers extend the stack: new measurement protocols become modules in the framework, and you validate the migrated ones on our QDm systems together with them.

  • Document the framework and hand it over so the team runs it on its own after your internship.

 

What is expected of you

  • Enrolled in or recently graduated from a degree program in computer science, software engineering, computational engineering, physics or electrical engineering with a strong software focus.

  • Available full time for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

  • Python is your working language: you structure packages, write type hints and tests, and have refactored or consolidated code you did not write.

  • Git and CI are routine for you, and you know how to make hardware-dependent code testable: mocked instruments, recorded data and simulation, with runs on real hardware as a separate stage.

  • AI coding agents are part of how you work, and you check their output the way you check your own.

  • You review code and take review well, you can agree on a common interface with engineers who each prefer their own solution, and you treat your colleagues as your users.

  • Fluent in English. On-site in Munich.

Experience with instrument control or lab automation in Python, with frameworks such as qudi, QCoDeS or PyMeasure, or contributions to open-source projects are a plus, not required. What we want you to bring is the patience to read code you did not write and the discipline to leave it better structured than you found it.

Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

  • Mentoring: An experienced colleague from the team mentors you throughout your internship.

  • Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

  • Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

  • Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 24 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

About us

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

Die Rolle

Unser Kernprodukt Konsentas ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

  • Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

  • Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

Nach 6 Monaten …

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für unsere Azubis eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

About The Exploration Company

At The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable orbital space vehicle that aims to eventually be refuelled in orbit, carrying cargo and potentially humans in the long run. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its engine, which is why we develop our own propulsion systems, aiming for the highest level of efficiency and reliability.

Role Summary

We are seeking a Junior Engine Control System & Monitoring Engineer to join the engine control and monitoring team of Storm, our high-thrust LOX/LCH4 cryogenic rocket engine. Working alongside senior control engineers, you will develop and test control and monitoring algorithms, work with the engine functional models provided by the functional team, contribute to setting up the controller development environment, and help verify the controller through Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop testing and during engine test campaigns. This is an entry-level, hands-on role for a recent graduate with strong control fundamentals who wants to learn on real hardware and progressively grow into full ownership of safety-critical engine control functions.

Key responsibilities:

1. Control & Monitoring Algorithm Development

• Design and implement engine control and monitoring algorithms, following the software team's rules, guidelines and auto-coding practices.

• Contribute to the definition of the engine regulation strategy (thrust and mixture ratio control, chill-down, start-up and shutdown transients) together with functional and system engineers.

• Support the definition of control and monitoring requirements for engine subsystems (valves, pumps, sensors, controller, software).

2. Simulation & Controller Development Environment

• Contribute to setting up the controller development environment: toolchain, model and code configuration management, auto-coding chain, and the MiL/SiL/HiL simulation and test infrastructure.

• Integrate the engine functional models delivered by the functional team (turbopumps, valves, combustion devices, cryogenic feed lines; steady-state, transient and chill-down) into the control design and simulation environment, deriving simplified or linearised models for controller synthesis where needed.

• Run closed-loop simulations to assess controller performance, stability margins and robustness to model uncertainties.

• Feed test results back to the functional team to support model correlation, and flag model limitations that matter for control.

3. Health Monitoring & Fault Management

• Contribute to the engine monitoring strategy that assesses the health status of the engine and its subsystems (combustion chamber, turbopumps, valves…).

• Implement fault detection and sensor validation logic for both real-time protection and post-test analysis.

• Support failure mode analyses (FMEA) and the management of failure modes, paving the way for engine reusability.

4. Validation, Testing & Documentation

• Prepare and run Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop (MiL, SiL, HiL) test campaigns to verify the control and monitoring functions at each step, from Simulink model to embedded code on target hardware.

• Support Storm engine and component cryogenic (LOX/LCH4) test campaigns: test preparation, on-site support, data processing and post-test analysis.

• Produce clear development documentation: specifications, test procedures, test reports and justification files.

• Master's degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace, Electrical, Control or Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Solid fundamentals in control theory, both classical and modern (state-space, robustness, digital control).

• Practical use of MATLAB/Simulink and Python through coursework or projects; basic knowledge of C/C++.

• Basic understanding of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics, and a strong interest in cryogenic propulsion and turbomachinery.

• Fluent in English.

Nice to Have:

• Exposure to MiL/SiL/HiL testing or real-time embedded systems.

• Experience with auto-coding from Simulink models.

• Familiarity with safety-critical design practices, reliability engineering or failure mode analysis.

• Interest or experience in data science applied to health monitoring and anomaly detection.

• Knowledge of space standards (ECSS, MIL-STD, NASA-HBK…).

Skills & Behaviours:

description:
Help shape the future of robotics in construction.

ABOUT XYZ REALITY

XYZ Reality created the world’s first and only engineering-grade augmented reality solution, purpose-built for the construction industry. Our holographic technology sits within The Atom, a smart, site-safe headset and hardhat, and is used on live projects to ensure schemes are delivered on time and on budget.

XYZ has grown to over 150 staff across the UK, US and Europe, and works with mission-critical organisations and construction companies to deliver major projects.

THE ROLE

Construction sites are some of the hardest environments for robot autonomy: they change every day and are full of clutter, obstacles and people. XYZ Reality’s robotics programme is extending our technology toward robots that can operate reliably in them, from autonomous data collection and construction progress capture through to executing construction tasks.

We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to make that real. You’ll work hands-on with robot hardware in our London office, using a modern stack (ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, learning-based control), and see your work tested in real construction environments, not just in simulation.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role focused on robot software and algorithmic control, backed by a good working knowledge of robot hardware. If you have strong robotics fundamentals from an MSc, PhD or applied research group, love making systems work on real robots, and want your ideas to shape the direction of a programme, we want to hear from you.

This is an office-based role at our London site in Angel, Islington.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Integrate robots with XYZ’s software, bringing up ROS / ROS 2 interfaces, robot control, sensors, compute and data flows, and building repeatable tools for bring-up, configuration, logging and monitoring.

  • Establish reliable baseline control and develop task-specific behaviours for navigation, positioning and capture, training and tuning control policies in simulation and validating them on hardware.

  • Develop localisation-aware path planning, waypoint execution and obstacle handling, working with project and site teams to turn work plans and BIM-derived locations into robot missions.

  • Integrate capture payloads so images, pose, timing and mission status flow reliably into XYZ’s construction progress workflows, working with navigation, SLAM and perception colleagues.

  • Design test scenarios and measure mission completion, coverage, localisation quality, intervention, recovery and repeatability, improving the system through measured iterations.

  • Bring technical expertise and new ideas to the programme, comparing scripted, motion-planning and learning-based approaches and helping shape what comes next.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • MSc or PhD in Robotics, Controls, Computer Science, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent applied robotics experience. Industry experience is not required.

  • Hands-on experience building, programming or directly controlling a physical robot, from an academic project, research lab or industry.

  • Strong Python and C++, practical ROS experience (ideally ROS 2) and working knowledge of kinematics, coordinate frames, feedback control, state estimation, path planning and robot hardware.

  • Experience training or tuning robot control policies (e.g. reinforcement or imitation learning) using NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim or similar tools, with a rigorous experimental approach.

  • The right to work in the UK. We’re unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

KEY EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

  • ROS / ROS 2, Python & C++

  • Robot control, kinematics, state estimation & path planning

  • NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim, reinforcement or imitation learning

  • Sim-to-real transfer on physical hardware (desirable)

  • Navigation, SLAM, perception & sensor fusion (desirable)

  • Mobile or field robotics, BIM/CAD or construction technology (desirable)

description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!
